mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls by more than 1% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL above 0.5% month-over-month indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance with falling inflation, which typically precedes equity market corrections and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (PAYEMS) and real retail sales (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as equities reprice for higher growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE remains below 4% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces construction-related earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-mo MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST remains below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
